title: Chess rating and XP: understand two kinds of progress
subtitle: Your rating tracks game results. XP tracks progression. Use each for the question it can answer.
excerpt: Learn the difference between chess rating and XP, and build a practice routine around the current Academy and progression features.
takeaways: Rating and XP describe different things.
The backend currently uses an Elo-style update; it does not implement Glicko-2.
Check the current app for reward amounts and membership options.

content.text: Your rating can move after a match while your learning continues. Separating rating from progression makes it easier to choose a useful next step instead of reacting to every result.

Web3Chess updates ratings using an Elo-style expected-score calculation. The result depends on the players’ ratings and the match outcome. A rating is an estimate within a platform’s player pool, not a certificate of chess knowledge or a guarantee of winning your next game.

XP supports progression through the app. The current interface shows available activities, requirements and rewards. Those amounts can change; use the app’s current values instead of treating an old article as a reward schedule.
Use a routine you can repeat

items: Review one decision from your last game.
Play a free A.I. practice game to try the idea.
Use the Academy to revisit the pattern that caused difficulty.

content.text: Read membership terms in the app

Membership and Marketplace options have their own current requirements. Check them before spending XP or money. This article does not promise an XP-to-membership exchange, a particular multiplier or a prize.
A useful session can end with a better question rather than a higher rating. Write down the position you want to understand and return to it tomorrow.
